sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Commercial Agricultural Full-Spectrum LED Fixtures

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 30 May 1984, as amended by the Protocol of 2 November 2013)
France–Hong Kong SAR Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and on Capital (signed 21 October 2010)
France–Singapore Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 9 September 2009)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI; France is a signatory, in force for French covered tax agreements)
European Union–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (political conclusion of December 2020; not yet in force — ratification currently suspended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Articles L.561-46 to L.561-52 of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Loi n° 2016-731 (Sapin II) of 3 December 2016; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 and Décret n° 2020-204 of 5 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Décret of 2 August 2023 restricting RBE access to legitimate-interest holders; Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (Anti-Money Laundering Regulation), applicable from 10 July 2027.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (RBE access restricted to competent authorities and obliged entities; public disclosure limited to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest per the 2023 decree — not a publicly browsable register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / current company extract of the ultimate foreign corporate shareholder (e.g., PRC business licence excerpt)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies register / State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (France and the shareholder's jurisdiction are parties to the 1961 Hague Convention); consular legalization only in lieu for non-contracting issuing states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade or tax registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the issuing state's accession to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (pouvoir) in favour of the representative executing the SARL's articles of association (statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's or representative's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternatively executed directly before a French notaire if signed in France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passport and proof of residential address for each proposed gérant and each UBO above 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the document holder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille where French banks or the registrar require legalization of foreign certified copies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax clearance / good-standing certificate of the foreign corporate shareholder (no outstanding fiscal debts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the shareholder's country of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization per issuing state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Article L.561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier and the EU AML framework: (i) PEP identification of any UBO or gérant holding a prominent public function, with enhanced due diligence (EDD) and senior-management approval; (ii) sanctions screening against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists (accepted French policy benchmark), French asset-freeze decrees issued by the Ministère de l'Économie, and Tracfin enquiries; (iii) adverse-media and source-of-funds verification for the capital contribution and ongoing business; (iv) documentation retained under the risk-based approach (RBA) applicable to a low-risk standard manufacturing company (ISIC 2740).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Direction générale des entreprises (DGE); official registry extract and RCS verification via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr); national registral base and identifier issuance administered by INPI under the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be written in French or in any other language using Latin characters; non-Latin corporate names must be transliterated into Latin script for RNE/RCS registration. The name must be distinctive, non-descriptive of the activity alone, lawful, and compliant with Article 1835 of the Civil Code and Article L.123-9 of the Commercial Code; it may contain only standard typographic characters and must not reproduce, in a confusing manner, the registered name of any third party.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Banquier — reserved to credit institutions licensed by the ACPR
Assurance / Assureur / Mutuelle — reserved to insurance and mutual companies authorized by the ACPR
Bourse / Chambre de Commerce / Chambre de Métiers — protected expressions of regulated institutions
République / France / National / État — misleading official-sounding tokens subject to State opposition
Notaire / Avocat / Huissier / Commissaire de justice — reserved to regulated legal professionals
Gendarme / Police / Impôts / Douanes — deceptive public-authority denomination tokens
Fiduciaire / SCPI / OPCVM — reserved to licensed financial intermediaries

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) and R.223-1 to R.223-31; Civil Code Article 1846-1; Law No. 2019-486 (PACTE) abolishing the minimum capital threshold.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (commercial court registry), accessed through Infogreffe or the relevant local commercial court registry; Kbis extract is the official corporate identity certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier unique d'immatriculation containing the signed articles of association (statuts) and the official M0 form, filed with the Greffe via Infogreffe; registration is evidenced by the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital. Cash contributions must be subscribed in full and paid up to at least 20% at incorporation or such higher fraction as required by the articles; funds may be deposited with a French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and the depositary attestation must be filed. Contributions in kind must be fully paid up and assessed by a statutory auditor unless a derogation applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole/multiple shareholders, acting in accordance with the articles of association, hereby resolve: (1) the share capital is subscribed and the specified contributions are approved and paid as required by law; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address], France; (3) [Name], having accepted office as Gérant, is appointed as legal representative for the full term of the company; (4) the Gérant is authorized to open bank accounts and sign the registration documents; (5) any one of the shareholders is authorized to publish the mandated legal notice and to complete all formalities before the commercial registry and other authorities. This resolution becomes effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-drafting and execution of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel; notary only if a real-property contribution is made or if the parties elect notarial execution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SARL statuts in French or as a bilingual French/English document containing the corporate name, corporate purpose, share capital, registered office, duration, contributions, rights attached to shares, and management provisions. All shareholders must sign each page. If in-kind contributions are made, annex the statutory auditor's valuation report. If cash capital is used, initiate the depositary attestation in parallel.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each shareholder
Proof of residential address of shareholders
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify the draft statuts to comply with legal objections, obtain re-signature of all shareholders, and if already filed, submit amended statuts through a subsequent extraordinary resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French-established credit institution, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, in the name of the company in formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account or an escrow account for the company in formation; deposit the subscribed cash capital; obtain a depositary certificate (attestation de dépôt de capital) identifying the company in formation, the amount deposited, and the signatory shareholders. The certificate must be delivered to the Greffe as part of the incorporation file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary certificate contains a name mismatch or incorrect amount, request the bank to reissue a corrected attestation before filing; if the bank refuses, select another institution and re-deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved in the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a legal notice in an approved JAL specifying the corporate form, corporate name, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and identity of the Gérant. Obtain the publisher's attestation of publication (attestation de parution). Publication must occur before the Greffe filing.
required_dossiers: Attestation de parution issued by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is defective under Articles R.210-4 and R.210-6 of the Commercial Code, publish a corrected notice and obtain a new attestation before presenting the file to the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing incorporation dossier with the commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through Infogreffe or directly at the local commercial registry office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 form, attach the signed statuts, depositary attestation, legal announcement attestation, proof of registered office, identity documents, and any mandatory power of attorney. Submit the full dossier electronically or physically and pay the registry fee. The Greffe will check legal compliance and proceed with registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if a representative signs
Identity and signature evidence of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Greffe's request for supplementary documents or corrections within the indicated deadline; amend the statuts if necessary and refile; appeal an unlawful refusal before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and issuance of Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the RCS assigns a SIREN number and issues the Kbis extract. Verify that the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, and Gérant as stated on the Kbis are accurate and match the filed documents.
required_dossiers: Internal verification checklist against filed statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a rectification of the Kbis extract from the Greffe by submitting a correction request with supporting evidence; any delay in issuance should be escalated through Infogreffe customer remedies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, URSSAF, DREETS, and DREAL according to the activation plan and premises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Kbis issuance, INRSE automatically generates SIRET and activation identifiers. If hiring will occur, open a social declaration account with URSSAF. If the manufacturing premises fall under environmental classification, file the ICPE declaration or registration with the relevant prefecture and complete the occupational health and safety records.
required_dossiers: Lease, ownership deed, or domiciliation contract for the registered office and production site
Employer registration details, if hiring staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct classification or registration data through the online business portal or directly with the relevant authority; if the ICPE self-classification is rejected, submit a formal declaration using the official form and provide technical supporting materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general commercial operating licence is required for LED fixture manufacturing under Article L.123-1-2 of the Commercial Code; however, an ICPE environmental declaration or registration (Déclaration/Enregistrement d'installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement) may be required for the production site. Product conformity remains subject to CE marking and applicable electrical and EMC standards.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires through DREAL and the local prefecture.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full environmental impact assessment is generally not required for a standard LED fixture assembly line below regulatory capacity thresholds. The activity is normally subject to a simplified ICPE declaration or registration under the French Environmental Code; if the site reaches higher hazardous substance or surface-treatment thresholds, an environmental authorisation (autorisation environnementale) under Articles L.181-1 et seq. is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with the local municipality's sewerage discharge regulations and any prefectural order, including pH limits, temperature, and suspended solids; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from soldering or cleaning operations must remain below the applicable thresholds under Directive 2010/75/EU; hazardous waste, waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE), and packaging waste must be handled under registered waste tracking manifests (bordereaux de suivi des déchets).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification requires an inspection by the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) and compliance with ERP or ICPE fire codes depending on building occupancy; production premises must have electrical installation certificates, grounding checks, and structural load clearance for storage and assembly areas; the employer must prepare the document unique d'évaluation des risques (DUER) and arrange occupational medical surveillance for workers exposed to soldering fumes, noise, and electrical hazards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the impots.gouv.fr portal; business formation and tax-ID issuance coordinated through the Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated under the CCI/CMA network for CFE functions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the French SARL online via the Guichet Unique portal, filing the M0 form and required statutes, to obtain SIREN, SIRET (with NIC), APE/NAF code 2740Z, and the statutory Kbis extract. Step 2: INSEE automatically transmits the registration to the DGFiP, which assigns the French EU VAT number (n° TVA intracommunautaire formatted FR + 11 digits). Step 3: For non-EU foreign entities that are not incorporated in France but perform taxable French supplies: file DGFiP Form No. 15537, appoint a DGFiP-approved fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) under Article 289 A of the CGI, and obtain a direct foreign-operator VAT number from the DGFiP; no SIRET is strictly required for such registration, but a French customs ID may be needed for imports. Step 4: Register for the corporate income tax regime (Impôt sur les Sociétés) via the tax office (SIE) and for the CET (CFE/CVAE transitional rules) where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a commercial manufacturing SARL is subject to French corporate income tax (IS) at a 25% standard reduced to 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs; no pass-through default. Territorial scope: French-resident entity taxed on French and foreign-source income with full liability; no tax-exempt zone status (no derogatory French free-zone applicable to a standard SARL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Option for the transparent/partnership regime (impôt sur le revenu) under Article 239 bis AA CGI for a maximum of 5 fiscal years, available only to SMEs with fewer than 50 employees and annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million; this is the only French check-the-box-like election for SARLs (no true US-style check-the-box). Hybrid mismatch adjustments under Articles 209-0 B and 212 bis C CGI (ATAD implementation) require French characterization to mirror EU classification rules and may override entity elections where mismatches cause double non-taxation; no other statutory entity-taxation elections apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_note: The 15% reduced IS rate is available only on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit, subject to EU SMB thresholds, and assumes the SARL is a small or middle-size enterprise for IS purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A French-established SARL must register for VAT upon formation regardless of turnover volume. For non-established EU suppliers: mandatory local VAT registration once intra-EU distance sales exceed EUR 10,000/year (OMP regime) or for all B2B supplies at any value. For non-EU suppliers: no VAT exemption threshold applies; registration is required from the first taxable supply in France. The domestic 'franchise en base de TVA' threshold (EUR 85,000 for goods; EUR 37,500 for services, updated for 2023-2025) is not applicable to a commercial manufacturing SARL because an invoice-exempt franchise is incompatible with export and intra-community zero-rating and input VAT claims on raw materials; the SARL must be a fully registered VAT operator.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has adopted a mandatory national e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (Ordonnance 2021-1190 and Decree 2022-1299). Phased deadlines: large and mid-size enterprises are required to receive and issue structured electronic invoices (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) from 1 September 2026, with small enterprises including SARLs compliant from 1 September 2027. Invoices must be exchanged through the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation) or a DGFiP-registered partner dematerialization platform (PDP). E-reporting (données de transaction et de paiement) is mandatory for B2B, B2C, and cross-border supplies, transmitted to DGFiP via the PPF in near-real-time; full pre-clearance is not yet applied but the reform permits DGFiP digital control of invoice data. No physical digital stamp is required, but a validated transmission receipt (Ack) is the compliance record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported to destinations outside the European Union are zero-rated (exonération à droit à déduction) under Article 262-I-1° CGI, provided the export is physically proven within three months of the date of the supply by a customs export declaration (DAU) or equivalent, and the goods leave the EU. Intra-EU supplies of the LED grow-light fixtures to a taxable person holding a valid French or other EU VAT number may be zero-rated under Article 262 ter CGI, subject to the customer's VAT ID, the intra-EU transport evidence, and the filing of the French Recapitulative Statement (DEB/DES). Eligibility is lost if the export proof is not obtained by the 3-month deadline, in which case French VAT at 20% becomes payable on the invoice and must be remitted to the tax authority.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU - Document Administratif Unique) lodged via DELTA G or ECS system, providing the MRN (Movement Reference Number) as the primary export proof
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), CMR transport document, or multimodal transport contract evidencing dispatch outside the EU (or intra-EU transport for zero-rating under Art. 262 ter CGI)

Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Inward Bank Transfer Confirmation (Swift MT103 / Airwallex settlement receipt) evidencing FX proceeds, retained prudentially for the 180-day repatriation benchmark and for transfer pricing and customs audit defense

Commercial Invoice with the zero-rating reference (Article 262-I-1° or 262 ter CGI) and delivery terms (Incoterms), plus Export Packing List and signed Delivery Receipt / POD for cross-border traceability
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may reassess VAT within the standard three-year statutory limitation period from the end of the filing year (Article L.169 Livre des Procédures Fiscales); the period is extended to six years for omitted/undisclosed operations and to ten years where fraudulent intent or abusive behaviors (manœuvres frauduleuses) are proven. Where export zero-rating is claimed without valid proof within three months, the VAT is immediately clawed back at 20% plus monthly late interest of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI); deliberate under-declaration or misstatement attracts a 40% penalty (manquement délibéré), rising to 80% for abusive fraud, plus possible criminal penalties. On intra-EU zero-rating, missing customer VAT ID, absent transport evidence, or late/incorrect DEB filings result in VAT reassessment and the same penalty scale. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days without documented commercial justification may also trigger transfer-pricing scrutiny under Article 57 CGI and French balance-of-payments reporting penalties for statistical breaches related to FX proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France participates in the euro area; the euro is fully and freely convertible under Article 63 TFEU. Capital account and current account transactions with non-EU counterparties are liberalized; no prior exchange-control authorization is required for profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation, subject to EU financial sanctions screening and French AML notification obligations. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to corporate tax documentation, a 25% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-treaty jurisdictions (reduced to 10% under the France-China DTT), and standard bank documentary checks; all payments may be made without currency conversion restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no holding timeline for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts held with a Banque de France-approved credit institution, or freely converted into euro. However, for balance-of-payments statistics, exporters must submit a monthly declaration (bulletin de déclaration) to the Banque de France covering cross-border transactions exceeding the applicable regulatory threshold, with the statement deadline falling on the 15th working day of the following month; precise origin and destination data must be retained for 10 years.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for payment execution, multi-currency treasury, and FX conversion; Medium for the main operating bank relationship. Airwallex, operating under an EU-recognised EMI or passporting arrangement with ACPR notification, can provide a French IBAN, SWIFT/SEPA routing, and local collection accounts for cross-border trade settlements. Legal constraints: an EMI may not grant credit, must safeguard client funds in low-risk assets, cannot provide capital escrow attestation required for French SARL funding, and must be registered or notified with the ACPR before servicing French-resident clients; full licensed banking services remain conclusively provided by credit institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for non-resident directors at Tier 1 French banks at account opening, unless the bank expressly adopts remote video-identification under Article R561-5-3 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Banks such as BNP Paribas and Société Générale typically require a physical or video interview with at least one authorised signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner(s); certified passport copies, apostilled corporate documents, and a notarised instruction letter are mandatory. Remote onboarding is legally possible for eligible corporate clients but is imposed only selectively by French Tier 1 banks, and the account opening decision remains for the Compliance Department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholding or UBO domiciled outside France/EEA
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the SARL's articles of association; Kbis extract; beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaire Effectif); corporate resolution authorising account opening; passport copies of all UBOs; proof of residential address; personal and corporate bank references; group organisational chart; audited annual financial statements or opening balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows inconsistent with SME revenue profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts, purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, bill of lading/CMR documentation, customs declaration (ENS/IM9), Incoterms confirmation, forecast cash-flow statement, and a detailed business plan demonstrating the horticultural LED grow-light export cycle.

Completed sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening results; counterparty beneficial-owner attestation; export licence documentation; end-customer declaration; dual-use or goods classification confirmation showing the LED fixtures are not controlled items; payment-chain description.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party or split payments from non-contractual accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tripartite payment instruction letters, legal explanation for the payment split, beneficiary identification, underlying trade invoices, transport documents, and CFO/CEO signed attestation of commercial reasonableness.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of digital EMI or foreign acquirer accounts before French bank account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EMI licence certificate or passporting notice, safeguarding attestation from the EMI, transaction trail, FX confirmation tickets, and reconciliation of all incoming/outgoing funds to the underlying contract.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires an SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer denominated in EUR to the French beneficiary account (FR76 IBAN) at a licensed French credit institution. The remittance must carry purpose code CAP or EQUI, and in field 70/72 a plain statement 'Equity capital contribution to FR_SARL'; the ultimate originator and beneficiary must be fully identified. For non-EU shareholder injection, the French entity must file an inward FDI statistical declaration with the Banque de France within 20 days of the transfer if the transaction is above the regulatory threshold; a bank capital-attestation certificate (attestation de dépôt de capital) is prepared for registration purposes only if formation capital is being deposited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements flow primarily over SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA counterparties, and SEPA SCT (ISO 20022) instruments for intra-EU payments. Documentary commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 are the preferred secured rail for horticultural LED fixture exports, with receiving banks examining bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, and certificates of origin. Airwallex virtual account rails may be used for forward aggregation and multi-currency disbursement, but each currency must respect its local AML reporting threshold and the French exporter must keep underlying shipping and customs records for 10 years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without deliverable FX market access
Currency options or collars deemed economically hedged to an underlying commercial trade

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the register of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filed with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accompanied by the annual return of entity information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry); data transmitted to the French Tax Administration (DGFiP) and INSEE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary of the company's registration in the RCS, or within 60 days of any change in beneficial ownership or registered details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine up to €15,000 plus potential imprisonment; registry may initiate administrative dissolution or strike-off proceedings for persistent non-compliance; inability to obtain Kbis extract blocks commercial transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (Comptes Annuels) comprising balance sheet, profit and loss account, and notes, approved by shareholders and filed with the commercial court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry); transmitted to the French Tax Administration (DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the end of the fiscal year; filing with the registry within one month of shareholder approval; standard calendar-year filers: filed by September 30 for the preceding December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of corporate income tax due per month, plus fixed late-filing fines up to €10,000; failure to file may trigger audits and criminal penalties for management (up to €75,000 and 5 years' imprisonment)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Déclaration de Résultat – Form 2065 and supporting schedules 2050 to 2059) for Entity-Level Taxation SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline: May 3 for calendar-year taxpayers; online filing requires an additional 15-day extension (May 18); non-corporate electronic filers may file by May 18
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of owed tax after formal notice, 40% base penalty, and 80% for abusive bad faith; default interest of 0.20% per month; penalties may be reduced for first-time filers with good faith

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dividend and distribution declaration (Section 117 bis, Form 2561) and gross-up reporting for shareholder payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually with the corporate income tax return; copy of the distribution decision filed with the tax authority within two months of the shareholder meeting by April 15 of the following year if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report distributions triggers a fine of €250 per missing or incomplete statement; taxable penalties plus 0.40% monthly interest on unpaid withholding taxes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual property tax declaration (Déclaration de Taxe Foncière – Form 6704) and business premises contribution declaration (Déclaration de CFE) covering commercial registered office or production facilities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Local Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declarations filed annually by May 15 for the following tax year; tax assessed and payable by December 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of assessed tax due; failure to file may result in summary assessment based on estimated rental values and additional 40% bad-faith penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll and social security reconciliation (Déclaration Sociale Nominative – DSN) monthly/annual filings and annual statement of social contributions (PAS) for any French employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF (Caisse Nationale) and French Tax Administration (DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly DSN by the 5th of the following month; annual social declarations submitted with the final DSN of the year by December 15; no separate annual paper statement required for electronic filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incomplete DSN filings subject to penalties up to 1.5% of reported gross wages per infraction; repeated failures may trigger criminal sanctions and employment inspector interventions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual vehicles and company asset usage declaration (Form 2855 – Déclaration de suivi de l'utilisation des véhicules) where corporate vehicles or emissions-relevant assets are held
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually by the corporate income tax filing deadline (May 3 or May 18 for online filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of €500 per incomplete or missing declaration plus penalties under Article 1728 of the French General Tax Code; may trigger additional audits on company car usage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual certification of registered office address and company secretary/registered agent confirmation (Mise à jour de l'extrait Kbis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Required whenever any corporate detail changes, then updated within one month; annual confirmation of unchanged details is recommended at each RCS anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Outdated information in the RCS may invalidate the Kbis extract and prevent bank account opening, public procurement bids, or VAT registration amendments; subject to administrative strike-off procedures, fines up to €15,000, and loss of limited liability protection

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (Commissaire aux Comptes) is required if the SARL exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total > €4,000,000; annual turnover > €8,000,000; average employee headcount > 50; alternatively, audit is mandatory if the company holds more than 20% of a parent group's consolidated control, is the parent of a subgroup, or exceeds 150 employees and €18,000,000 turnover. Below thresholds, the company may opt for a voluntary audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG) as codified in the Code de Commerce and the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulation; consolidated groups may apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU, where applicable to the parent entity hierarchy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SARL must maintain a register of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) at its registered office. The register is filed with the RCS and must be annually confirmed or updated within 60 days of any transfer of shares or change in control. Share transfers must be recorded in the company's securities register (Registre de Transfert d'Actions), and a written confirmation of the updated beneficial owner details must be provided to the registry with supporting identification documents; non-compliance blocks the company's Kbis extract issuance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Associés) – recording all share transfers and pledges
Register of Directors (Registre des Décisions des Gérants) – recording management resolutions
Minute Book (Registre des Procès-Verbaux d'Assemblées Générales) – binding shareholder resolutions, including annual meeting approved accounts

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: €600–€1,500 typically for commercial registered-office services from a legal or corporate agent in Paris or major industrial regions
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €3,500–€8,500 estimated for a full statutory audit engagement under French GAAP for a mid-sized SARL with manufacturing operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate for FY2025 on taxable profits of French-resident sociétés; a reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of profit for qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced corporate income tax rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit (conditions: turnover below EUR 10,000,000, paid-up capital fully released, and at least 50% of equity held directly by individuals or qualifying entities). Research Tax Credit (CIR) of 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure up to an annual ceiling of EUR 100,000,000, applicable to horticultural LED engineering, photometry testing and agronomical validation. Innovation Tax Credit (CII) of 20% of eligible innovation expenses up to EUR 400,000 per annum, covering prototyping, preclinical and technical feasibility work distinct from R&D. The 3.3% social surcharge on corporate income tax (contribution sociale sur l'IS) applies only where the annual corporate income tax due exceeds EUR 763,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward (no statutory time limit); annual deduction of carried-forward deficits is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000 in any given year. Optional loss carryback (report en arrière) is limited to the immediately preceding fiscal year, capped at EUR 1,000,000 of deficit, and reimbursed over five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultat) filed electronically with annexes 2050 to 2059 via the French professional e-file portal EFP (Espace Fiscal Professionnel, efp.impots.gouv.fr) or EDI transmission in XML. Mandatory electronic filing applies to all French companies regardless of size. A separate balanced-sheet return is integrated with the 2065-SD package; the annual VAT return (CA3) and the annual statement of transactions with related parties (Formulaire 2258-SD) are coordinated filings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing of the 2065-SD package; corporation tax is prepaid through four quarterly instalments (acomptes) within the fiscal year, followed by a balance payment at the conclusion of the annual filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: the return is due on the second business day following 1 May (in practice 3 May of the following year). For non-calendar fiscal years, the return must be filed within three months of the balance-sheet date. Quarterly instalments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, legal form (SARL), SIREN, SIRET, NAF/APE code 2740Z, address of the registered office and of the principal establishment, and the fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL is the taxpayer; non-resident shareholders have no direct filing duty. Non-resident managing directors must obtain French tax registration and mandate an approved fiscal representative or an authorised accountant to operate the EFP credentials.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total turnover (chiffre d'affaires) net of VAT and settlement discounts, disaggregated by domestic sales, intra-EU dispatches and exports of horticultural full-spectrum LED fixtures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all French-source turnover of the SARL; export sales to third countries are included at gross value with proof of export kept in the supporting record. No special non-resident entry regime applies because the entity is French-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax add-backs (réintégrations): non-deductible expenses such as excess depreciation, entertainment expenses, fines, and 30% of luxury passenger car depreciation; also add-back of excessive interest paid to related parties (thin-capitalisation rules).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any intra-group royalty or interest payments disallowed under Article 57 CGI and Article 212 CGI where the related party is a non-resident affiliate and the arm's-length proof is missing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result before loss offset (résultat fiscal avant imputation): computed as accounting profit adjusted for réintégrations and déductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computation must be consistent with the audited financial statements; non-resident managers remain jointly responsible for accurate treatment of related-party transactions with overseas LED component suppliers or group buying offices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carried-forward tax losses deducted this year (déficits reportables imputés), limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable excess, with proof of loss schedule in Annex 2058-B.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deficits generated by the French SARL are eligible; deficits of foreign affiliates or of foreign permanent establishments cannot be imputed unless attributed to a French branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Portion of annual taxable profit eligible for the 15% reduced rate, capped at EUR 42,500 per fiscal year if the SME criteria (turnover under EUR 10,000,000 and 95% capital held by individuals) are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident corporate shareholder controls the SARL, the small-business reduced rate may be denied; the 25% standard rate applies to the full taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of gross corporate income tax at 15%/25%, deduction of tax credits (CIR, CII, foreign tax credits), addition of the 3.3% social surcharge where applicable, and subtraction of quarterly instalments already paid to arrive at the balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits for withholding taxes suffered abroad require documentary proof and treaty entitlement; the CIR/CII credit must be supported by a Form 2069-A. The final balance is debited electronically from the company's bank account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared material transactions with related enterprises and with non-resident enterprises located in preferential tax regimes: purchases, sales, royalties, management fees, interest, loans and guarantees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with Hong Kong, Singapore, or other low-tax related purchasers must be priced at arm's length; any omission of this annex leads to the automatic rejection of deductions and a EUR 150 fixed penalty per missing statement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the tax due where the return is filed within 30 days of a formal notice, 10% beyond 30 days; 40% penalty for deliberate late filing or intentional inaccuracy; 80% penalty for fraudulent conduct or abuse of law. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month on all unpaid tax. A fixed penalty of EUR 150 applies for failure to annex the balance sheet or the related-party form; EUR 5 per omitted or incorrect field on certain mandatory schedules. Criminal exposure under Article 1741 CGI applies to concealed turnover.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under domestic law (Article 119 bis-2 CGI) on dividends distributed by a French SARL to non-resident corporate shareholders. The levy is applied at the moment the dividend is declared payable, unless the recipient simultaneously invokes the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a double-tax treaty. Distributions to resident corporate shareholders are exempt from withholding under the parent-subsidiary participation exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a reduced or zero treaty rate, the foreign shareholder must (i) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the home tax administration for the relevant calendar year, (ii) establish direct or indirect ownership of the holding period and share percentage, and (iii) submit the certificate and a claim form (Formulaire 5016 / 5008) to the French paying SARL before or at the time of payment so that the payer applies the treaty rate at source. Where tax was over-withheld, the shareholder may file a refund claim (réclamation contentieuse) with the DGFiP within three years of the distribution, providing the TRC, dividend vouchers, and the written treaty interpretation justifying the reduction. For EU/EEA parent companies applying the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (zero withholding), France requires a holding of at least 10% of the SARL's capital, unless a 5% tier is available under domestic law as revised following CJEU precedent; the parent must be effectively subject to corporate tax without option in its EU state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding under Article 182 B CGI is 33.33% on patent royalties, know-how fees, trademark and copyright payments made by a French SARL to non-resident licensors. Treaty rates commonly reduce this to 5% (industrial royalties) or 0-10% (copyright or cultural royalties); the France-Hong Kong DTA, if applicable, reduces royalty withholding to 5% for patents/trademarks and 3% for industrial equipment. Interest: French domestic law exempts arm's-length interest paid to non-resident lenders from withholding (Article 125 A CGI) unless the recipient is established in a Non-Cooperative State or Territory (ETNC), in which case a 75% withholding applies; treaty overrides reduce or eliminate this. Payments to related offshore financing vehicles are additionally scrutinised under the thin-capitalisation and interest-deduction cap rules of Article 212 CGI.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File and Local File documentation under Article L.13 AA of the French Tax Procedures Book (LPF) is mandatory where the French entity or the French group head achieves annual turnover or gross total assets of at least EUR 400,000,000. Simplified documentation obligations may apply between EUR 50,000,000 and EUR 400,000,000; enterprises with turnover and gross assets below EUR 50,000,000 are exempt from the formal transfer-pricing file but must still be able to demonstrate the arm's-length character of intra-group transactions on audit. Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR) applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000, with the CbCR return filed via the DGFiP and exchanged automatically. The obligation extends to non-resident-owned French entities that control or are controlled by a group meeting the threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France is not an offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) jurisdiction, but a robust economic substance doctrine applies through the general anti-abuse rule known as 'abus de droit' (Article L.64 LPF), the fiction of 'société écran' (letterbox company), and Article 57 CGI on profit shifting to related enterprises. A French SARL that lacks staff, premises, managerial decision-making, real commercial activity, and risk-taking for its LED grow-light manufacturing and distribution may be disregarded, with its profits re-attributed to the real foreign beneficiary. The EU ATAD rules (interest limitation, CFC regime, exit taxation, and GAAR) and the DAC6 mandatory disclosure regime further penalise artificial arrangements lacking genuine substance. The CFC regime under Article 209 B CGI can re-attract passive income of low-taxed controlled subsidiaries or foreign branches where the French company does not demonstrate real economic activity in the foreign jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration or dissimulation of turnover of horticultural LED grow-light sales in the 2065 return, issuance of false or manual invoices outside the invoicing system, widespread cash or unreported bank receipts, or systematic undervaluation of exports to related offshore resellers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI: criminal fine up to EUR 750,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; aggravated circumstances (committed in organised gang, involving accounts held outside France or shell companies) raise the penalty to EUR 2,000,000 and 7 years of imprisonment. Tax adjustments carry an 80% fraudulent-filing penalty plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers are prosecuted as principals or co-authors; penalties include imprisonment, fine, confiscation of assets, withdrawal of passports and judicial travel bans. The corporate veil can be pierced where the SARL is a sole conduit, entailing joint and several restitution of the evaded tax, social security contributions, and damages to the Treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Structure (société écran and abuse de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation of a French SARL without real premises, employees, inventory, or management, used solely as an invoicing and contracting shell to route LED hardware sales made by a foreign principal, or to localise profits in France while actual control and decision-making remain abroad, with profits repatriated via fictitious management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article L.64 LPF the tax administration sets aside the entire arrangement, re-characterises the transactions at the economic owner's level, and denies all corresponding deductions; an 80% abuse-of-law penalty is imposed under Article 1729(b) CGI plus late-payment interest. The shell may be administratively struck off and its VAT registration cancelled retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors risk personal joint liability for the re-characterised tax debt, unlimited civil restitution in insolvency proceedings (action en comblement de passif), and criminal conviction for complicity in tax fraud; the court may issue travel bans and prohibit the directors from managing any commercial company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payments of non-arm's-length royalties, service fees, or inflated component prices to a Hong Kong, Singapore, or other low-tax related purchasing entity, or deliberate mispricing of goods to shift profits outside the French taxable base while leaving the SARL with no residual margin for its manufacturing functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment under Article 57 CGI with the re-allocation of profits to the French SARL; application of the normal arm's-length methods (CUP, resale price, TNMM or profit split); 40% penalty for deliberate failure to file or document related-party transactions, rising to 80% where abuse of law is proven. The related-party statement (Annex 2258-SD) is exclusionary: omission bars the deduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign or approve sham pricing documentation are personally liable for the restitution of adjusted tax and penalties; the criminal courts may impose imprisonment for complicity in tax evasion, freeze bank accounts, and order travel bans pending trial. Directors of foreign parent entities involved in the scheme may be prosecuted in absentia and subject to extradition requests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the beneficial owner declaration (RBE) with the commercial court registry, concealment of the ultimate non-resident shareholder through undisclosed nominee arrangements, or failure to file the Country-by-Country Report for a group exceeding EUR 750,000,000 consolidated revenue, together with laundering of tax-fraud proceeds through the corporate bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBE omission is punishable by a fine up to EUR 7,500 and/or 6 months' imprisonment under the French Monetary and Financial Code; the registry may also refuse deposit of annual accounts, effectively freezing the company's legal existence. CbC non-filing exposes the group to an administrative penalty of up to EUR 100,000 and automatic exchange flagging. Laundering of tax-evasion proceeds carries 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, increased to 10 years and EUR 750,000 for habitual or organised laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners and de facto managers are jointly criminally liable; sanctions include confiscation of corporate and personal assets, closure of bank accounts, travel bans, and prohibition orders. The corporate veil is pierced to reach directors who orchestrated layering, conversion, or transfer of dirty funds through the SARL's Swift/TT and Airwallex payment rails.
